data.one_liner: SQLite plugin for Flutter supporting iOS, Android and MacOS.
data.what_it_does: Provides a self-contained, embedded SQL database engine for Flutter applications. Offers helpers for insert, query, update, and delete operations along with transaction and batch support.
use_when: You need a robust relational database with complex SQL queries on device.
You want support for transactions and batch operations.
You are targeting iOS, Android, and macOS platforms natively.
avoid_when: You are looking for a simple key-value store without SQL queries.
You prefer compile-time safe database queries via code generation.
strengths: Mature and widely used in the Flutter ecosystem.
Supports transactions and batch execution for performance.
Executes database operations in a background thread on iOS and Android.
weaknesses: Concurrent read and write transactions are not supported due to SQLite limitations.
Does not support complex types like DateTime or bool natively out of the box.
data.setup_notes: Add to pubspec.yaml via flutter pub add sqflite. Linux, Windows, and Web require additional packages like sqflite_common_ffi or sqflite_common_ffi_web.

alternatives.name: drift
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want type-safe SQL queries and code generation.

alternatives.name: hive_ce
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer a lightweight key-value NoSQL database.

alternatives.name: shared_preferences
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you only need to store simple configuration key-value pairs.
